idiom_name: struct-of-function-pointers contract + init function taking the dependency struct
implementation_notes: C has no classes, so the role structure is built by hand: the service interface becomes a struct of function pointers (a hand-rolled vtable), the consumer holds a const pointer to it plus an opaque context pointer, and an init/create function takes the dependency as a parameter instead of calling into a concrete module. What replaces the injector is the composition step in main or an app_init function that builds the concrete structs and passes them down; link-time substitution of a fake implementation (or conditional compilation) is the fallback test seam. The classic configuration/container structure is not worth reproducing in C - there is no reflection to drive it, so keep the wiring explicit and small.
pitfalls: An unset or NULL function pointer crashes at the call site: initialise every member and check before use.
Sharing one mutable context across consumers couples them; give each consumer its own context or document ownership.
Static or global service pointers undo the injection - the same module then cannot serve two configurations in one process.
